description: Experimental GT assembly orders seeded from Marsh 2013 + exp_gt_v2.2

complexes.name: Hemoglobin
complexes.notes: alpha nucleates, then alpha2, then beta, then beta2

complexes.name: Subtilisin Carlsberg / Eglin C
complexes.source: Bode W et al. (1987) EMBO J 6(4):1111-1118
complexes.notes: Eglin C binds native, folded subtilisin. Protease is obligate seed — folds and is catalytically active before inhibitor association. Kinetics show inhibitor binds to pre-folded enzyme.

complexes.name: Alpha-Chymotrypsin / BPTI
complexes.source: Ruhlmann A et al. (1973) J Mol Biol 77(3):417-436
complexes.notes: BPTI binds the active-site cleft of folded chymotrypsin. Serine protease fold is obligate first; inhibitor association is second. Canonical Kunitz-domain inhibitor mechanism.

complexes.name: Subtilisin BPN' / Streptomyces SSI
complexes.source: Hirono S et al. (1984) J Mol Biol 178(3):389-413
complexes.notes: SSI wraps around the substrate-binding groove of folded subtilisin. Protease is the constitutive scaffold; SSI binds post-fold.

complexes.name: Porcine Pancreatic Elastase / OMTKY3
complexes.source: Fujinaga M et al. (1987) J Mol Biol 195(2):397-418
complexes.notes: Turkey ovomucoid third domain binds the S1-S2 subsites of folded elastase. Serine protease is obligate seed; inhibitor is recruited second.

complexes.name: Subtilisin BPN' / Chymotrypsin Inhibitor 2
complexes.source: Jackson SE & Fersht AR (1991) Biochemistry 30(43):10436-10443; McPhalen CA & James MNG (1987) Biochemistry 26(1):261-269
complexes.notes: CI-2 binding mechanism well-characterised by phi-value analysis. Subtilisin is the obligate scaffold; CI-2 binds via a single-transition-state mechanism to the active-site cleft. 2SIC is the crystal structure of the subtilisin BPN' / CI-2 complex.

complexes.name: CDK2 / Cyclin A2
complexes.notes: CDK2 is constitutively expressed and exists as an inactive monomer. Cyclin A is cell-cycle regulated; its binding to CDK2 drives T-loop rearrangement and kinase activation. CDK2 is the obligate seed.

complexes.name: Colicin E9 DNase / Im9 Immunity Protein
complexes.source: Keeble AH et al. (2006) J Mol Biol 361(2):355-372
complexes.notes: Colicin E9 DNase domain folds independently and is expressed first in the colicin operon. Im9 binds with femtomolar affinity to inhibit DNase activity, providing self-immunity. DNase is obligate seed.

complexes.name: Beta/Gamma-Actin / DNase I
complexes.source: Bhatt D et al. (1997) FEBS Lett 412(1):131-136
complexes.notes: G-actin (monomeric actin) is the constitutively present cytoskeletal protein. DNase I traps actin monomers to prevent polymerisation; actin folds first and DNase I binds second. Chain A = actin, chain P = DNase I.

complexes.name: Triosephosphate Isomerase (TIM homodimer)
complexes.source: Waley SG (1973) Biochem J 135(1):165-172; Casal JI et al. (1987)
complexes.notes: TIM barrel homodimer with well-characterised sequential assembly. In vitro reconstitution experiments show sequential monomer addition; each TIM barrel subunit folds independently and then dimerises.

complexes.name: p53 DNA-Binding Domain Tetramer
complexes.source: Clore GM et al. (1994) Science 265(5170):386-391; Rajagopalan S et al. (2010)
complexes.notes: p53 assembles as dimer-of-dimers. Two stable homodimers (AB and CD) form via antiparallel beta-strand interface first, then two dimers associate via helix-helix interface to form tetramer. Dimers are the kinetically stable intermediates. 2OCJ contains all 4 chains in the asymmetric unit.

complexes.name: Interferon Alpha-2A / IFNAR2 Extracellular Domain
complexes.source: Piehler J & Schreiber G (1999) J Mol Biol 289(1):57-67
complexes.notes: Type I interferon signalling requires sequential receptor binding: IFN-alpha first engages IFNAR2 with high affinity (KD ~1 nM), then recruits IFNAR1. IFNAR2 binding is the obligate first step. Chain X = IFN-alpha, chain Y = IFNAR2.

complexes.name: Glucoamylase / Acarbose inhibitor domain
complexes.notes: Enzyme-inhibitor complex; glucoamylase folds as a stable enzyme before pseudo-tetrasaccharide binding. Chain F = glucoamylase, chain G = acarbose binding domain.

complexes.name: Heterotrimeric G protein (Gα·Gβ·Gγ)
complexes.source: Gilman AG (1987) Annu Rev Biochem 56:615; Muntz KH et al. (1992) J Biol Chem 267:23796; Wall MA et al. (1995) Cell 83:1047
complexes.notes: Gβγ forms an obligate heterodimer prior to Gα association. Gβ and Gγ are co-dependent — neither is stable alone in native form. Gα-GDP binds preformed Gβγ to complete the heterotrimer. Chain A=Gαi1, B=Gβ1, G=Gγ2.
